title: Homepage — developer playbook copy experiments
content:
Purpose:
Quick working doc to iterate hero and above-the-fold messaging aimed specifically at engineering and ML platform buyers. We want copy that reduces time-to-first-call-to-action for engineers: sign up, run a sample request, or request a Dedicated trial. This is intentionally scrappy — keep options minimal, measurable, and developer-first.

Target audience (primary / secondary):
- Primary: backend/ML engineers building product features (search, assistants, agents) who care about latency, cost, and predictable SLAs.
- Secondary: platform/infra leads evaluating a standardized inference runtime (Dedicated & Private buyers).

One-sentence positioning to test (control concept):
- "A predictable inference runtime for engineers — fast, cost-transparent, and cloud‑agnostic."

Core benefit buckets to surface above the fold (short):
- Predictable performance: throughput and p99 latency you can rely on.
- Predictable unit economics: clear per-token economics and tooling to lower cost.
- One API, any deployment: hosted, reserved Dedicated capacity, or Private.

Hero copy variants (short, developer tone) — pick 3 to test:
1) "Stop chasing infrastructure. Ship LLM features with an inference runtime built for production."
2) "Same API. Any infra. Predictable latency and cost for real products."
3) "From prototype to SLA-backed inference — fast, low-friction, and cost-aware."

Micro-variants (word swaps / short tests):
- "inference runtime" vs "inference platform" vs "serving runtime"
- "predictable latency" vs "SLA-backed latency" vs "p99 latency guarantees"

Subhead/supporting lines to pair with hero (short bullets):
- "Ship language features without operating the stack: streaming, KV-caching, function calling"
- "Profiler-grade observability: per-route cost, traceable regressions, and rollout tools"
- "Autoscale and dedicated pools for production load — bring your own keying and VPC"

CTA variants (primary) to test:
- "Start a free workload"
- "Run a sample request"
- "Request a Dedicated trial"

CTA variants (secondary):
- "See latency & cost benchmarks"
- "Compare deployment options"

Above-the-fold layout hypotheses (quick tests):
- H1: Hero + 3 micro-benefits + primary CTA + benchmark strip (latency/cost) beneath the fold.
- H2: Hero + interactive code snippet (curl + Node) + primary CTA + "Trusted by" logos.
- H3: Hero + short 3-step flow "signup → run sample → pin model" emphasizing quick time-to-value.

Competitive notes (bulleted, do not publish):
- OpenAI: great for prototyping, strong model quality and developer UX but opaque cost for high-throughput production and limited private deployment options.
- Anthropic / Claude: safety and model families are differentiators; still platform-managed with less focus on per-token unit economics for custom infra.
- AWS Bedrock / GCP: enterprise reach and infra control, but slower onboarding and less opinionated inference optimizations tuned for latency per-dollar.
- Self-hosted runtimes (Kagome-style): full control but heavy ops burden — key message: we remove that ops tax while preserving infra flexibility.

Key proof points to call out on page (short bullets):
- Benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 tail for sample models on GPU+Quantized variants (link to deeper benchmark page).
- Customer story (short): "moved from prototype to 10M tokens/day with 40% cost reduction after adopting Dedicated pools" (obscured name until case study approved).
- Platform features: per-route cost breakdown, rollout canaries, KV prefix caching, quantization profiles.

Evidence and microcopy for feature callouts (one-liners):
- "Per-request cost and latency in the Console — trace every token."
- "Automatic prefix/KV caching reduces repeat-token compute by X% (workload dependent)."
- "Canary rollouts and automatic fallback keep apps online during model flakiness."

Metrics/hypotheses to measure (what success looks like):
- Short-term: +18–25% lift in "run sample request" clicks for code-snippet variant vs control.
- Mid-term: +12% conversion from run-sample to sign-up when benchmark strip is visible.
- Qualitative: engineers cite "cost predictability" or "dedicated capacity" in 40% of post-trial feedback.

A/B test plan (practical):
- Week 0: implement A (control) and B1 (interactive code) + B2 (benchmark strip).
- Traffic split: 25% B1, 25% B2, 50% control. Run for 14 days or until 1,000 unique engineering visits per arm. Primary metric = click on primary CTA; secondary = signup conversion within 7 days.

Quick ownership / engineering needs:
- Marketing: implement copy and micro-variations + assets for benchmark strip.
- Growth: configure experiment in Optimizely / LaunchDarkly.
- Dev: include the runnable code snippet (curl + node) that executes against sandbox API key and returns a tiny streaming response.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Do we publish full numerical benchmarks or just relative % lifts? Legal and performance team need sign-off.
- Which real customer case study can be cleared for homepage-level callout? (CS owning).
- Should we prioritize developer interactive flow over immediate trust signals (logos/benchmarks)? hypothesis: interactive flow increases trial starts; trust signals increase enterprise lead form fills.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Pick hero variant A/B set by EOD Friday (Maya).
2) Growth to wire experiment and mock traffic allocation (Noah).
3) Engineering to build sandbox-run snippet & benchmark strip component (Riley).
4) Compile initial benchmark artifacts and legal checklist for public numbers (Ezra).

Notes to future reader: this doc is intentionally rough. Keep iterations small, measure fast, and prefer copy that reduces time-to-first-success for an engineer rather than high-level messaging that appeals primarily to procurement.

-- end of draft --
